transcript.text:
Playing The Village House and Bread Day at the Village Oven.

The Village House
Ah, my village house, it’s like a piece of my heart. Built with mud bricks and a thatched roof, it stood tall through many seasons. The walls, though simple, held the whispers of generations. Every morning, the sun would paint the room in golden hues, and the smell of fresh bread from the oven would fill the air. We children would gather around the fire at night, listening to grandparents tell tales of old times. That house wasn’t just a shelter; it was a living memory of our ancestors, a testament to our resilience and love. 

Bread Day at the Village Oven
Bread day was a special day in our village. Early in the morning, women would gather dough they had prepared over several days. The air would be filled with the scent of rising dough and anticipation. We’d walk to the communal oven, our baskets laden with loaves shaped by skilled hands. The oven, built from stone and clay, stood as a centerpiece of our community. As the bread baked, the crackling fire and the warmth would bring us closer. Sharing that first loaf, warm and fresh, was a bond that transcended words. It was a day of unity, flavor, and tradition passed down through generations.

It was lovely to hear my own voice again. My grandchildren in Ankara are so curious about our past; they always ask me to tell them more when I visit.
